card.name: Some of which: severity qualifiers after reactions
card.fires_on: Words like some, which, have or with that come right after a list of serious adverse reactions and begin a clause saying how severe some cases were. Mostly in warnings sections such as Hypersensitivity Reactions.

modes.label: Some after a reaction
modes.description: The word some follows a named reaction and a comma, introducing a detail about some cases.
modes.example: Serious anaphylactic reactions,<< some>> following the first dose, have been reported

modes.label: Some of which
modes.description: The word which or have in the phrase some of which introduces an outcome such as fatal or life-threatening.
modes.example: some of<< which>> have resulted in death.

modes.label: Cases with
modes.description: The word with follows cases and introduces a finding.
modes.example: Cases<< with>> serum sodium lower than 110

card.writes: It promotes words meaning accompanied by or with, which suggests a clause adding an attached detail about severity.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a warning says that some of the reported reactions were severe, such as fatal or needing hospital care.
